ESV.1: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “Behold, we are your bone and flesh.
ESV.2: In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led out and brought in Israel. And the LORD said to you, ‘You shall be shepherd of my people Israel, and you shall be prince  over Israel.’”
ESV.3: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel.
ESV.4: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
ESV.5: At Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and at Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah thirty-three years.
ESV.6: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who said to David, “You will not come in here, but the blind and the lame will ward you off” — thinking, “David cannot come in here.”
ESV.7: Nevertheless, David took the stronghold of Zion, that is, the city of David.
ESV.8: And David said on that day, “Whoever would strike the Jebusites, let him get up the water shaft to attack ‘the lame and the blind,’ who are hated by David's soul.” Therefore it is said, “The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.”
ESV.9: And David lived in the stronghold and called it the city of David. And David built the city all around from the Millo inward.
ESV.10: And David became greater and greater, for the LORD, the God of hosts, was with him.
ESV.11: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, also carpenters and masons who built David a house.
ESV.12: And David knew that the LORD had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
ESV.13: And David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.
ESV.14: And these are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
ESV.17: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to search for David. But David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.
ESV.18: Now the Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
ESV.19: And David inquired of the LORD, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?” And the LORD said to David, “Go up, for I will certainly give the Philistines into your hand.”
ESV.20: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David defeated them there. And he said, “The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a breaking flood.” Therefore the name of that place is called Baal-perazim.
ESV.21: And the Philistines left their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.
ESV.22: And the Philistines came up yet again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
ESV.23: And when David inquired of the LORD, he said, “You shall not go up; go around to their rear, and come against them opposite the balsam trees.
ESV.24: And when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then rouse yourself, for then the LORD has gone out before you to strike down the army of the Philistines.”
ESV.25: And David did as the LORD commanded him, and struck down the Philistines from Geba to Gezer.

CSB17.1: All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron <sup>ⓚ</sup> and said, “Here we are, your own flesh and blood. <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.2: Even while Saul was king over us, you were the one who led us out to battle and brought us back. <sup>ⓜ</sup> The LORD also said to you, ‘You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be ruler over Israel.’”
CSB17.3: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron. King David made a covenant with them <sup>ⓝ</sup> at Hebron in the LORD’s presence, and they anointed David king over Israel.
CSB17.4: David was thirty years old when he began his reign; <sup>ⓐ</sup> he reigned forty years.
CSB17.5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
CSB17.6: The king and his men marched to Jerusalem against the Jebusites <sup>ⓑ</sup> who inhabited the land. The Jebusites had said to David: “You will never get in here. Even the blind and lame can repel you” thinking, “David can’t get in here.”
CSB17.7: Yet David did capture the stronghold of Zion, that is, the city of David. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.8: He said that day, “Whoever attacks the Jebusites must go through the water shaft to reach the lame and the blind who are despised by David.” <sup>[2]</sup> For this reason it is said, “The blind and the lame will never enter the house.” <sup>[3]</sup>
CSB17.9: David took up residence in the stronghold, which he named the city of David. He built it up all the way around from the supporting terraces inward.
CSB17.10: David became more and more powerful, <sup>ⓓ</sup> and the LORD God of Armies was with him. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.11: King Hiram of Tyre sent envoys to David; he also sent cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons, <sup>ⓕ</sup> and they built a palace for David.
CSB17.12: Then David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
CSB17.13: After he arrived from Hebron, David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
CSB17.14: These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, <sup>ⓖ</sup> Solomon,
CSB17.17: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, <sup>ⓘ</sup> they all went in search of David, but he heard about it and went down to the stronghold. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.18: So the Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
CSB17.19: Then David inquired of the LORD: <sup>ⓚ</sup> “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?” The LORD replied to David, “Attack, for I will certainly hand the Philistines over to you.”
CSB17.20: So David went to Baal-perazim and defeated them there and said, “Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me.” <sup>ⓛ</sup> Therefore, he named that place The Lord Bursts Out. <sup>[4]</sup>
CSB17.21: The Philistines abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them off.
CSB17.22: The Philistines came up again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
CSB17.23: So David inquired of the LORD, and he answered, “Do not attack directly, but circle around behind them and come at them opposite the balsam trees.
CSB17.24: When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, act decisively, for then the LORD will have gone out ahead of you to strike down the army of the Philistines.” <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.25: So David did exactly as the LORD commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.

NLT.1: Then all the tribes of Israel went to David at Hebron and told him, “We are your own flesh and blood.
NLT.2: In the past, when Saul was our king, you were the one who really led the forces of Israel. And the LORD told you, ‘You will be the shepherd of my people Israel. You will be Israel’s leader.’”
NLT.3: So there at Hebron, King David made a covenant before the LORD with all the elders of Israel. And they anointed him king of Israel.
NLT.4: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in all.
NLT.5: He had reigned over Judah from Hebron for seven years and six months, and from Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah for thirty-three years.
NLT.6: David then led his men to Jerusalem to fight against the Jebusites, the original inhabitants of the land who were living there. The Jebusites taunted David, saying, “You’ll never get in here! Even the blind and lame could keep you out!” For the Jebusites thought they were safe.
NLT.7: But David captured the fortress of Zion, which is now called the City of David.
NLT.8: On the day of the attack, David said to his troops, “I hate those ‘lame’ and ‘blind’ Jebusites. Whoever attacks them should strike by going into the city through the water tunnel. ” That is the origin of the saying, “The blind and the lame may not enter the house.”
NLT.9: So David made the fortress his home, and he called it the City of David. He extended the city, starting at the supporting terraces and working inward.
NLT.10: And David became more and more powerful, because the LORD God of Heaven’s Armies was with him.
NLT.11: Then King Hiram of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber and carpenters and stonemasons, and they built David a palace.
NLT.12: And David realized that the LORD had confirmed him as king over Israel and had blessed his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
NLT.13: After moving from Hebron to Jerusalem, David married more concubines and wives, and they had more sons and daughters.
NLT.14: These are the names of David’s sons who were born in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
NLT.17: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king of Israel, they mobilized all their forces to capture him. But David was told they were coming, so he went into the stronghold.
NLT.18: The Philistines arrived and spread out across the valley of Rephaim.
NLT.19: So David asked the LORD, “Should I go out to fight the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?” The LORD replied to David, “Yes, go ahead. I will certainly hand them over to you.”
NLT.20: So David went to Baal-perazim and defeated the Philistines there. “The LORD did it!” David exclaimed. “He burst through my enemies like a raging flood!” So he named that place Baal-perazim (which means “the Lord who bursts through”).
NLT.21: The Philistines had abandoned their idols there, so David and his men confiscated them.
NLT.22: But after a while the Philistines returned and again spread out across the valley of Rephaim.
NLT.23: And again David asked the LORD what to do. “Do not attack them straight on,” the LORD replied. “Instead, circle around behind and attack them near the poplar trees.
NLT.24: When you hear a sound like marching feet in the tops of the poplar trees, be on the alert! That will be the signal that the LORD is moving ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army.”
NLT.25: So David did what the LORD commanded, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

WEB.3: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron, and king David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Yahweh; and they anointed David king over Israel.

WEB.5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months; and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
WEB.6: The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spoke to David, saying, “The blind and the lame will keep you out of here”; thinking, “David can’t come in here.”
WEB.7: Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion. This is David’s city.
WEB.8: David said on that day, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him go up to the watercourse and strike the lame and the blind, who are hated by David’s soul.” Therefore they say, “The blind and the lame can’t come into the house.”
WEB.9: David lived in the stronghold, and called it David’s city. David built around from Millo and inward.
WEB.10: David grew greater and greater; for Yahweh, the God of Armies, was with him.
WEB.11: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar trees, carpenters, and masons; and they built David a house.
WEB.12: David perceived that Yahweh had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.
WEB.13: David took more concubines and wives for himself out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.
WEB.14: These are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
WEB.17: When the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David, but David heard about it and went down to the stronghold.
WEB.18: Now the Philistines had come and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
WEB.19: David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?” Yahweh said to David, “Go up; for I will certainly deliver the Philistines into your hand.”

WEB.22: The Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
WEB.23: When David inquired of Yahweh, he said, “You shall not go up. Circle around behind them, and attack them in front of the mulberry trees.
WEB.24: When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then stir yourself up; for then Yahweh has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
WEB.25: David did so, as Yahweh commanded him, and struck the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.

MSG.1: Before long all the tribes of Israel approached David in Hebron and said, "Look at us—your own flesh and blood!
MSG.2: In time past when Saul was our king, you're the one who really ran the country. Even then God said to you, 'You will shepherd my people Israel and you'll be the prince.' "
MSG.3: All the leaders of Israel met with King David at Hebron, and the king made a treaty with them in the presence of God. And so they anointed David king over Israel.
MSG.4: David was thirty years old when he became king, and ruled for forty years.
MSG.5: In Hebron he ruled Judah for seven and a half years. In Jerusalem he ruled all Israel and Judah for thirty-three years.
MSG.6: David and his men immediately set out for Jerusalem to take on the Jebusites, who lived in that country. But they said, "You might as well go home! Even the blind and the lame could keep you out. You can't get in here!" They had convinced themselves that David couldn't break through.
MSG.7: But David went right ahead and captured the fortress of Zion, known ever since as the City of David.
MSG.8: That day David said, "To get the best of these Jebusites, one must target the water system, not to mention this so-called lame and blind bunch that David hates." (In fact, he was so sick and tired of it, people coined the expression, "No lame and blind allowed in the palace.")
MSG.9: David made the fortress city his home and named it "City of David." He developed the city from the outside terraces inward.
MSG.10: David proceeded with a longer stride, a larger embrace since the God-of-the-Angel-Armies was with him.
MSG.11: It was at this time that Hiram, king of Tyre, sent messengers to David, along with timbers of cedar. He also sent carpenters and masons to build a house for David.
MSG.12: David took this as a sign that God had confirmed him as king of Israel, giving his kingship world prominence for the sake of Israel, his people.
MSG.13: David took on more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he left Hebron. And more sons and daughters were born to him.
MSG.14:
These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem:
Shammua,
Shobab,
Nathan,
Solomon,
MSG.17: When the Philistines got word that David had been made king over all Israel, they came on the hunt for him. David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.
MSG.18: When the Philistines arrived, they deployed their forces in Raphaim Valley.
MSG.19: Then David prayed to God: "Shall I go up and fight the Philistines? Will you help me beat them?"
MSG.20:
"Go up," God replied. "Count on me. I'll help you beat them."
David then went straight to Baal Perazim, and smashed them to pieces. Afterwards David said, "God exploded on my enemies like a gush of water." That's why David named the place Baal Perazim (The-Master-Who-Explodes).
MSG.21: The retreating Philistines dumped their idols, and David and his soldiers took them away.
MSG.22: Later there was a repeat performance. The Philistines came up again and deployed their troops in the Rephaim Valley.
MSG.23:
David again prayed to God.
This time God said, "Don't attack them head-on. Instead, circle around behind them and ambush them from the grove of sacred trees.
MSG.24: When you hear the sound of shuffling in the trees, get ready to move out. It's a signal that God is going ahead of you to smash the Philistine camp."
MSG.25: David did exactly what God told him. He routed the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.
